title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (Early and partial Late Show) on 1970-01-03
venue: Fillmore East (Early and partial Late Show)
source: SBD:MR> DAT> Cass.> DAT > CDRPLUS:1. Sound improved on d1t02 (Me & My Uncle)2. SBE's corrected and checked, new md5's generated.

ai_review.summary: Superb soundboard capture of the Jan 3 1970 Fillmore East show, highlighted by a knockout set with The Other One, Alligator and Mason’s Children soaring.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality soundboard tape that delivers clear, punchy mixes despite a few occasional cuts. Musically the performance is often described as "ridiculously good" – Pigpen dominates the first set while the second set erupts with The Other One, Alligator, Mason’s Children and a jam after drums that teases China Cat and We Bid You Goodnight. Reviewers rave about the energy, tightness and memorable moments, making this one of the standout 1970 shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive comments on both performance (standout jams, high energy) and recording quality (crisp soundboard with only minor mix issues) across many reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well‑balanced for a 1970 tape; several reviewers call it "Super 70' Soundboard" and note the organ is prominent. A few mention occasional cuts and Phil’s bass being low in the mix, but overall the audio is very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a high‑energy Morning Dew opening, heavy Pigpen presence in the first set (Hard to Handle, Alligator), then launches into a jam‑laden second set where The Other One drives the momentum and transitions flow smoothly through Uncle John's Band → Black Peter, with a memorable post‑drums jam.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his vocal intensity ('sings like it's his last time') and guitar tone described as perfect.
band_member_comments.Phil: One reviewer notes Phil’s bass sits low in the mix, possibly due to source material.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ (TC) is highlighted as being “really in the mix” with distinct flourishes; keyboards receive strong positive attention throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum section is commended for its tightness and a standout jam after drums that includes teases of China Cat Sunflower.
